text: Political forces distributed their seats in the new parliament, each will have a seat on the first row (27.04.2026 16:10)

At a meeting in the National Assembly building, political forces distributed their seats in the new 52nd parliament. There should be no disputes over chairs, tables, and offices; for us, this is a third-rate issue, Petar Vitanov from "Progressive Bulgaria" told journalists after the meeting.

Regarding the election of the Chairperson of the National Assembly, Vitanov said that good parliamentary practice requires the deputies to be informed before the first session. Even if we are ready, the last place I would say it is this early in front of the media, he noted. According to him, Galab Donev is a suitable candidate because he is sufficiently erudite and authoritative.

Vitanov pointed out that there is a huge problem related to justice. Urgent anti-crisis measures are needed to curb prices, and the funds under the Recovery and Resilience Plan are also at risk, he added.

The distribution was consensual; everyone showed understanding toward the arrangement. We are keeping a portion of our offices and vacating another for "Progressive Bulgaria," said Zhecho Stankov from GERB. A candidacy for Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly has not yet been discussed, nor has a joint choice for Speaker of Parliament been commented on, he commented.

All parties will have a seat in the front row, our parliamentary group will be on the far right, stated Nadezhda Yordanova from "We Continue the Change – Democratic Bulgaria" (PP-DB). No talks have been held with us by "Progressive Bulgaria" regarding the Speaker of the National Assembly, she added.

Regarding the candidate for Deputy Speaker of Parliament, Yordanova said that "Democratic Bulgaria's" proposal for the position is Gen. Atanas Atanasov. To a question about whether the group will stay together or split, she replied, "we face the task of being a constructive, effective, and active opposition force." It is a shared responsibility to provide a solution to the task of being an effective opposition force that guarantees Bulgaria's democratic pro-European path. Our proposal is to be in a joint group based on a clear coalition agreement, Yordanova added.

Asked whether she is ready to support Andrey Gyurov as a candidate for president, she replied that he is successful as an acting prime minister. I do not think it is appropriate to comment at this stage, she added.

The allocation went calmly; I think all parliamentary groups will be satisfied. Every group will be able to come to the rostrum of the National Assembly, said Miroslav Ivanov from PP-DB. "Progressive Bulgaria" are allocated in the center-left, he added. Our priorities remain as they have been so far - justice, high incomes, and a competitive business environment, Ivanov pointed out.

The more important question is what is happening with the state, whether we will change the Supreme Judicial Council (SJC), whether measures will be taken regarding inflation and rising prices, rather than the MPs' rooms, said Petar Petrov from "Vazrazhdane".

To a question about what agenda "Vazrazhdane" is entering with and whether it will support some of the bills or be entirely in opposition, Petrov indicated that the party will support the replacement of the SJC from the parliamentary quota, as well as legislative changes to stop inflation.
The fifty-second National Assembly will be convened on Thursday at 10:00 AM, said the president.
